title: New London man charged after federal investigators find heroin, cocaine, crack, Xanax pills in home - NewsBreak
text:
By William Gonzalez ,
6 hours ago
NEW LONDON, Conn. (WTNH) — A New London man has been charged with operating a drug factory after a search of his apartment resulted in the seizure of multiple narcotics, including Xanax, heroin and crack cocaine.
Nestor Pagan, 43, was arrested Wednesday after a group of investigators from the New London Police Department, Connecticut State Police and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) searched his apartment and found heroin, cocaine, crack cocaine, Xanax and multiple illicit firearms
Connecticut State Police asks for help identifying Tolland burglary suspect According to New London police, the search took place around 7:19 a.m. at his residence on Bank Street.
During the search, the investigators found 6.3 grams of heroin, 47.4 grams of cocaine, 69.1 grams of crack cocaine, 50 Xanax pills, cutting agents, digital scales, a 9mm pistol with no serial number, a .22 caliber pistol with an extended magazine, 53 9mm hollow-point rounds and 47 .22 caliber rounds.
Nestor Pagan of New London was charged with operating a drug factory after a group of investigators from the New London Police Department, Connecticut State Police and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) searched his apartment on Wednesday and found heroin, cocaine, crack cocaine, Xanax and multiple illicit firearms on Wednesday, April 29, 2026. Nestor Pagan of New London was charged with operating a drug factory after a group of investigators from the New London Police Department, Connecticut State Police and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) searched his apartment on Wednesday and found heroin, cocaine, crack cocaine, Xanax and multiple illicit firearms on Wednesday, April 29, 2026. Pagan was arrested and charged with four counts of narcotics possession, four counts of possession of narcotics with intent to sell, operating a drug factory, possession of drug paraphernalia, criminal firearm possession, alteration of a firearm identification, three counts of large-capacity magazine possession and assault weapon possession.
